about: Opponent brains V3 lays over V1's AI (src/brain.ts brainProfile): a row's knobs replace the same-named knobs of the opponent's own V1 profile at the fight's level (profileAt(opponent, level), src/fight/moves.ts); every knob the row leaves out stays V1's. data/fight.json `ai` names the row the fight plays; ?ai=v1 plays V1's profile untouched (today's fight). Row `novice` is V2's novice brain (frankendom-v2 data/behaviours.json brains[0], V2's default since 26 Oct). V2's brain.js is a port of V1's ai.ts decide() and its rows use V1's AiProfile names, so every field maps one to one, same meaning (V1 src/fight/moves.ts AiProfile, read in src/fight/ai.ts): reaction = ticks before a fresh swing is noticed; accuracy = timing precision of the answer (jitter); parry = chance a noticed swing is parried; dodge = chance it is rolled; aggression = attack cadence; pressure = share of non-punish attacks that are lights; discipline = stamina floor (% of the bar) under which he backs off; lapse = chance a noticed swing gets no answer; read = chance he guards the side the swing comes from. Dropped from V2: the row's `id` is kept as the row id only; V2's `defaults` (absent knobs) are V1's own absent rows already (moves-tables-defs.json), and V2's dials/read/fight tables are V1's ai rows, so none is copied. On the Centurion at level 18 the novice keeps his own knobs from moves-tables-defs.json own_knobs (tellReaction 15, braceHeavy 1, spamRun 5): his body, gladius, scutum, specials and look are the level-18 man's; only how he reads and answers is the novice's.
